newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish stocks leap 1.22 percent in low volume.
newsitem.headline: Turkish stocks leap 1.22 percent in low volume.

text.p: Turkish stock market index rose 1.22 percent on Monday amid selective activity.
The IMKB-100 index provisionally closed at 72,452.91, up 876.23 points from Friday's close.
Trade volume ended at 8.07 trillion lira, down from Friday's 8.4 trillion lira.
Brokers said a downward correction was expected during the week. The index's gains have totalled 11.85 percent since September 13.
"Depending upon daily technical indicators, the market awaits a correction since the last weekend. But it did not happen today," said Cem Yalcinkaya from Garanti Investment Bank.

"The lower-than-expected volume today approves the correction expectation. On the other hand, good weekly technical indicators have been indicating that the upward movement will keep on," Yalcinkaya added.
A medium-term uptrend had begun when the critical resistance at 70,000 was shattered amid fresh cash entry and economic optimism.
Brokers expect good nine-month profit prospects to keep the selective demand fresh in the coming days.
Of the 224 shares traded, 91 ended higher, 68 steady and 65 fell. The 85-share industrial index rose 1.18 percent at 79,281.77 and the 15-share financial index gained 1.34 percent at 64,593.46.
Shares of state-owned iron and steel producer Erdemir led the actives as it rose 100 lira to 9,900. A private bank Yapi Kredi bankasi was another active share, rising 100 lira to 2,300.
